title: Derived etale module pullback has the stalk at the image point
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $u:U\to T$ any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and $\bar v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. On the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], use the constant-coefficient module inverse image $u^*$ with $u^{-1}A_T\cong A_U$ and its exactness as in [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Use the unbounded derived categories of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the geometric stalks of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Write $D(u^*)$ for the functor induced by applying $u^*$ termwise, and $D(s_{\bar w})$ for the functor induced by the exact module stalk at a geometric point $\bar w$. There is a natural isomorphism of functors to $D(A)$
$$ D(s_{\bar v})\circ D(u^*)\ \cong\ D(s_{u\circ\bar v}). $$
For a representing complex $C$, this isomorphism is represented by the degreewise canonical inverse-image stalk comparisons
$$ (u^*C^n)_{\bar v}\xrightarrow{\sim} C^n_{u\circ\bar v}. $$
These maps are additive and $A$-linear and commute with the differentials and all morphisms of complexes; the displayed derived isomorphism is their descent through localization at quasi-isomorphisms. No boundedness, finiteness or hypothesis on $u$ beyond being a scheme morphism is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback), clauses (1) and (3), extended termwise to unbounded constant-coefficient module complexes and localized at quasi-isomorphisms

proof.text: Put $P=u^*$, $S=s_{\bar v}$ and $R=s_{u\circ\bar v}$. For an $A_T$-module sheaf $M$, [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of $PM$ with $u^{-1}M$, naturally in $M$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] to obtain the canonical additive isomorphism $c_M:S(PM)\xrightarrow{\sim}R(M)$, natural in module morphisms. It is $A$-linear: for $a\in A$, let $m_a:M\to M$ be multiplication by its constant section. Naturality of the abelian comparison gives $c_M\circ S(Pm_a)=R(m_a)\circ c_M$. The action-transport and constant-ring identification in [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] identify $Pm_a$ with multiplication by $a$ on $PM$; [lem-sfb-etale-stalk-constant-complex-exactness] identifies constant-ring stalks with $A$ with its ordinary action. Thus this equation is precisely $c_M(ax)=a c_M(x)$. Consequently $c:SP\xrightarrow{\sim}R$ is a natural isomorphism of functors to $A$-modules.

source.place: Tag 03Q1, lemma-stalk-pullback (3), with the constant-module action of prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact

proof.text: For any unbounded cochain complex $C$, define $(c_C)^n=c_{C^n}$. Naturality of the comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ], after the module identification just made, applied to $d_C^n:C^n\to C^{n+1}$ says $c_{C^{n+1}}\circ SP(d_C^n)=R(d_C^n)\circ c_{C^n}$. This is the chain-map equation. The inverse components satisfy the reverse equation by multiplying this equality by the two inverses, so $c_C$ is a chain isomorphism. For a chain map $h:C\to E$, the same naturality applied to each $h^n$ gives $c_E\circ SP(h)=R(h)\circ c_C$ degree by degree. These are exactly the degreewise canonical stalk comparisons, and their additivity and $A$-linearity are those established in step 1.

source.place: Tag 03Q1, lemma-stalk-pullback (3), with the constant-module action of prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact

proof.text: The functor $P$ is additive and exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. The stalk functors $S$ and $R$ are additive and exact by [lem-sfb-etale-stalk-constant-complex-exactness], applied to the two image geometric points. The composite $SP$ therefore preserves finite limits and finite colimits, by applying the two preservation properties successively. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to $P,S,R$ and $SP$. Their termwise functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms and induce $D(P),D(S),D(R)$ and $D(SP)$, with the comparison $a_{H,C}:D(H)(QC)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(C(H)C)$ for each $H$. In particular every complex, including an unbounded one, represents its image by termwise application.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor (3)-(4); stalk exactness is sites-modules.tex Tag 04EQ, lemma-stalk-exact-modules (1)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-exact-derived-natural-iso] to $c:SP\xrightarrow{\sim}R$ and [lem-sfb-exact-derived-composition] to $(P,S)$. Define the desired isomorphism to be $\alpha=D(c)\circ\mu_{P,S}^{-1}:D(S)D(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}D(R)$. To check its prescribed representative, put $\beta_C=a_{S,C(P)C}\circ D(S)(a_{P,C})$. The composition lemma gives $\beta_C\circ\mu_{P,S,QC}=a_{SP,C}$, whereas the natural-isomorphism lemma gives $a_{R,C}\circ D(c)_{QC}=Q(c_C)\circ a_{SP,C}$. Substitution yields $a_{R,C}\circ\alpha_{QC}=Q(c_C)\circ\beta_C$. Thus under the termwise representing identifications, $\alpha$ is exactly the localization of the chain isomorphism of step 2. Both cited lemmas give natural isomorphisms on the entire derived categories, so this comparison is natural for every derived morphism. All hypotheses used were exactness and the scheme morphism and geometric-point hypotheses; no boundedness, finiteness, or extra condition on $u$ has entered.

tool_uses.why: Ordinary abelian stalk comparison with its naturality and unit normalization; a generic etale-site tool, not a replacement of the preservation route.
Constant-module action transport and exact inverse image for any scheme morphism; the unit itself has no such site-level construction.
Exact additive module stalk and ordinary constant-ring scalar action for an arbitrary commutative ring; no preservation or purity theorem is taken from its unit.
Generic normalized composition of functors induced by exact functors, used solely to identify D(SP) with D(S)D(P).
